To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
perinatal DHA deficiency is associated with increased blood pressure in later life.
perinatal dietary n-3 polyunsaturated fat deficiency is associated with increased blood pressure in adult rats.
the perinatally n−3 PUFADeficient rats had significantly elevated blood pressures compared with the n−3 PUFDAffluent rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hypothesis that the development of high blood pressure in later life may be associated, in part, with a perinatal n-3 fatty acid deficiency.
the effects of n−6 and n−3 PUFAs on cardiovascular health and the mechanisms by which these nutrients influence the control of blood vessels and the heart.
the effects of n− 3 PUFA on the control of blood pressures and blood pressure regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
n−3 PUFAs are beneficial for blood pressure and cardiovascular health, and that a perinatal deficiency of n−3 PUFUAs may be associated with increased blood pressure later in the rat.
perinatal DHA deficiency is a risk factor for later hypertension.
perinatal n-3 PUFA deficiency may be associated with hypertension in later life.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the perinatology of n−3 PUFAs may have a long-term influence on blood pressure control in the adult.
perinatal dietary n−3 PUFAs are important in the long-term control of blood pressure.

perinatal DHA deficiency leads to increased blood pressure in adult rats, and that the mechanism by which DHA exerts its antihypertension effect is not related to the fatty acid composition of the tissue phospholipids in the hypothalamic area.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the perinental period is a sensitive time for programming the cardiovascular system.
the perinatally acquired fatty acid profile may have long-term implications for the control of blood pressures in later life.
n−3 PUFAs, especially DHA, are essential for optimal development of the cardiovascular system.
